about: Every source this site draws on, with how each link was checked. confirmed: an AI model (Claude, or research agents it directed) opened the link and the content matched. That is not the same as a person reading it; sources Robert has read himself carry a readBy date. person: no AI model opened the page, often because the site blocks automated readers, so Robert opened it in a browser; whether he has read it is recorded separately in readBy. unopened: the link comes from an official index or search, but no one has opened it yet. no-link: listed as background reading, with no public link recorded yet. checkedOn is the first day sources were checked and lastCheckedOn the latest.

sources.title: Brazilian Data Protection Law (LGPD), Law No. 13,709 of August 14, 2018, as amended by Law No. 13,853/2019 (English translation)
sources.publisher: Agência Nacional de Proteção de Dados (ANPD), Government of Brazil
sources.note: Robert read Chapter III, Articles 17 to 22, which include the parts this site cites, in his saved copy.
sources.summary: Article 20 gives the data subject the right to request a review of decisions made solely by automated processing, and clear information on the criteria and procedures used, within trade and industrial secrecy. Article 19 requires a complete answer to a data request within 15 days.

sources.title: Article 20: Right to Review Decisions Based on Automated Processing of Personal Data
sources.note: The page does not say whether its translation is official. The ANPD translation is the primary source.
sources.summary: English text of LGPD Article 20: the right to request a review of solely automated decisions affecting personal, professional, consumer, or credit profiles, and clear information on the criteria and procedures used.

sources.title: Legge 23 settembre 2025, n. 132: Disposizioni e deleghe al Governo in materia di intelligenza artificiale
sources.publisher: Gazzetta Ufficiale della Repubblica Italiana, Serie Generale n. 223
sources.note: Full text of Articles 1 to 28 read from the official issue. Robert read all 28 articles through an unofficial English translation made with AI help (Claude); the Italian text in the Gazzetta Ufficiale remains the authoritative version.
sources.summary: Italy's national AI law. Art. 4: children under 14 need a parent's consent to use AI. Art. 7: in health care, patients have the right to be told when AI is used, and the decision always stays with the doctor. Art. 11: employers must inform workers. Art. 13: professionals must explain their AI systems to clients in clear, simple language. Art. 14: in public administration, the person stays solely responsible. Art. 20: AgID and ACN are the national AI authorities; the Garante keeps its powers.

sources.title: Article L311-3-1 - Code des relations entre le public et l'administration
sources.note: Full article text read; in force since 9 October 2016, created by Loi n° 2016-1321 (République numérique), art. 4.
sources.summary: When a public body makes an individual decision using an algorithm, the decision must say so. On request, the body must share the algorithm's rules and main features.

sources.title: Article R311-3-1-2 - Code des relations entre le public et l'administration
sources.note: Full article text read; in force since 1 September 2017 (Décret n° 2017-330).
sources.summary: On request, and in a form people can understand, the public body must explain how much the algorithm counted, what data it used and where the data came from, the parameters and their weights as applied to the person, and what the processing did.

sources.title: Article 47 - Loi n° 78-17 du 6 janvier 1978 relative à l'informatique, aux fichiers et aux libertés
sources.note: Full article text read (version in force since 1 June 2019).
sources.summary: No court decision judging a person's behavior may rest on automated profiling of their personality. Fully automated decisions with serious effects are allowed only in narrow cases with explanation duties, and never when a public body rules on an administrative appeal.

sources.title: Article 5 - LOI n° 2023-451 du 9 juin 2023 visant à encadrer l'influence commerciale et à lutter contre les dérives des influenceurs sur les réseaux sociaux
sources.note: Consolidated article read (version in force since 8 November 2024).
sources.summary: Paid influencers must label AI-generated images of a face or body "Images virtuelles", or with an equivalent notice suited to the format.

sources.title: Vos droits à l'intervention humaine face à votre profilage ou à une décision automatisée
sources.summary: Where a fully automated decision with serious effects is allowed, you can be told about it, learn its logic, challenge it, and ask a person to review it.

sources.title: Entrée en vigueur du règlement européen sur l'IA : les premières questions-réponses de la CNIL
sources.note: Q&A read as updated on 17 August 2026.
sources.summary: The CNIL says the EU AI Act adds to the GDPR and does not replace it, that it still fully enforces the GDPR for AI, and that each EU country organizes its own AI Act oversight.

sources.note: Official gazette PDF read: Art. 1 (§ 491a BGB), Art. 3 (BDSG § 30, deletion of § 31, new § 37a), Art. 16 (in force 20 November 2026).
sources.summary: Germany's consumer credit law. From 20 November 2026 a new credit-scoring rule (§ 37a BDSG) bans some data from scores, gives a right to learn the main factors, and a right to challenge a score-based decision and have a person decide.

sources.title: Beschlussempfehlung und Bericht des Ausschusses für Recht und Verbraucherschutz zu dem Gesetzentwurf zur Umsetzung der Richtlinie (EU) 2023/2225 über Verbraucherkreditverträge (Drucksache 21/5381)

sources.title: Using Consumer Reports: What Landlords Need to Know
sources.note: Read on 29 September 2026.
sources.summary: Tenant background check reports are consumer reports. A landlord who turns someone down because of one must name the company that supplied it, say that company didn't make the decision, and tell the applicant about their right to a free copy within 60 days and to dispute errors.

sources.title: Housing Discrimination Under the Fair Housing Act
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD)
sources.note: Read on 29 September 2026.
sources.summary: The Fair Housing Act bans housing discrimination because of race, color, national origin, religion, sex, familial status, or disability.

sources.title: Learn About FHEO's Process to Report and Investigate Housing Discrimination
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD)
sources.note: Read on 29 September 2026: file within one year of the last date of the alleged discrimination; online, by phone, e-mail, or mail; no fees when the government brings a case.
sources.summary: How to report housing discrimination to HUD, and the one-year deadline.

sources.title: 15 U.S. Code § 1681a: Definitions; rules of construction
sources.publisher: Legal Information Institute, Cornell Law School
sources.note: Read on 29 September 2026: subsection (k)(1)(B)(i). Cornell's LII publishes the U.S. Code; the official text is at uscode.house.gov.
sources.summary: An "adverse action" includes refusing or cancelling insurance, charging more for it, or cutting or worsening its coverage, so the credit-report notice rules apply to insurers too.

sources.title: How to File a Complaint
sources.note: Read on 29 September 2026: try the insurer first; state insurance departments investigate complaints for free; links to every state's department.
sources.summary: How to take an insurance complaint to your state's department of insurance, for free, after trying the insurer first.

sources.title: Bima Bharosa: our process
sources.publisher: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI)
sources.note: Read on 29 September 2026: complaints are attended to within 14 days; if unresolved beyond 15 days or the answer is unsatisfactory, you may go to the Insurance Ombudsman; no payment is asked at any stage.
sources.summary: India's free insurance complaint portal, with a path to the Insurance Ombudsman if the insurer doesn't resolve the complaint.

sources.title: 15 U.S. Code § 1666: Correction of billing errors
sources.publisher: Legal Information Institute, Cornell Law School
sources.note: Read on 29 September 2026. Cornell's LII publishes the U.S. Code; the official text is at uscode.house.gov.
sources.summary: You can dispute a credit card billing error in writing within 60 days of the statement, including for goods or services not delivered as agreed. The card company must acknowledge within 30 days and resolve it within two billing cycles, and no later than 90 days.

sources.title: Guarantees and returns
sources.note: Read on 29 September 2026.
sources.summary: You can cancel most online and other distance purchases within 14 days without giving a reason; the period extends to 12 months if the seller didn't tell you about this right. Some things, such as tickets, perishable goods, and custom-made items, are excluded.

sources.title: Changing your mind about something you've bought
sources.note: Read on 29 September 2026. Citizens Advice is an independent charity, not a regulator.
sources.summary: Things bought without seeing them in person usually come with a 14-day cooling-off period, starting the day after delivery, and nothing needs to be wrong with them. The seller must refund within 14 days of getting the item back or proof it was posted.

sources.title: Getting your money back if you paid by card or PayPal
sources.note: Read on 29 September 2026. Citizens Advice is an independent charity, not a regulator.
sources.summary: Credit card purchases of more than £100 and up to £30,000 per item can be claimed back from the card company under section 75; otherwise, ask for a chargeback. If refused, the Financial Ombudsman can look at the case.

sources.title: Lei nº 8.078, de 11 de setembro de 1990 (Código de Defesa do Consumidor), art. 49
sources.note: Read on 29 September 2026.
sources.summary: For purchases made outside a shop, such as online or by phone, the consumer can withdraw within 7 days of signing or receiving the product, and everything paid must be returned at once.

sources.title: Decreto nº 11.034, de 5 de abril de 2022 (Serviço de Atendimento ao Consumidor)
sources.note: Read on 29 September 2026: applies to services regulated by the federal government (art. 1); phone service with a human for at least 8 hours a day, and complaint and cancellation in the first menu (art. 5); answers within 7 calendar days (art. 13).
sources.summary: Customer service rules for federally regulated services: a phone line with a human available at least eight hours a day, complaint and cancellation options in the first menu, and answers within seven days.

sources.title: User rights under the Digital Services Act
sources.note: Read on 29 September 2026 (page last updated 17 July 2026).
sources.summary: Platforms must explain their content moderation decisions to affected users (Article 17); users can ask for a review through the platform's internal complaint system (Article 20), go to a certified dispute settlement body (Article 21), complain to their national Digital Services Coordinator (Article 53), and always go to court.

sources.title: Out-of-court dispute settlement bodies under the Digital Services Act (DSA)
sources.note: Read on 29 September 2026: ten certified bodies listed.
sources.summary: Certified bodies that settle disputes over platform moderation decisions. They are free or low-cost for users, the platform pays all fees if it loses, and their decisions aren't binding, but platforms must engage in good faith.

sources.title: California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA)
sources.publisher: State of California Department of Justice, Office of the Attorney General
sources.note: Read on 29 September 2026.
sources.summary: Californians can ask large businesses what personal information they collect and how they use it, free, up to twice a year. Businesses must answer within 45 days (up to 90 with notice) and can't treat people worse for asking.

sources.title: What will the FTC's enforcement of the TAKE IT DOWN Act mean for you?
sources.note: Read on 29 September 2026.
sources.summary: Since 19 May 2026, platforms must offer a way to request removal of intimate images shared without consent, including AI-made deepfakes, and remove them and known identical copies within 48 hours. People can tell the FTC at TakeItDown.ftc.gov if a platform doesn't comply.

sources.title: Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3)
sources.note: Read on 29 September 2026: filing is free; the IC3 never contacts people for money.
sources.summary: The FBI's central place to report internet crime, including scams, for free. Reports may be passed to law enforcement.

sources.title: Our new APP fraud reimbursement protections
sources.note: Read on 29 September 2026.
sources.summary: Since 7 October 2024, people tricked into sending money by UK bank transfer (Faster Payments or CHAPS) are usually reimbursed, up to £85,000, if they claim within 13 months; banks may apply a £100 excess. The exceptions for complicity or gross negligence don't apply to vulnerable people.

sources.title: Guia de implementação dos procedimentos de devolução no Pix, com ênfase no Mecanismo Especial de Devolução
sources.note: Read on 29 September 2026 (version 4.3): contest in the bank's app within 80 days of the Pix; allowed even if the payer authorised it with a password or biometrics; recovery depends on funds still being in the receiving account.
sources.summary: How people tricked into sending a Pix can contest it through their bank to try to get the money back, within 80 days, even when they authorised the payment themselves.

sources.title: National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal
sources.publisher: Ministry of Home Affairs, Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C)
sources.note: Read on 29 September 2026: helpline 1930 for financial cyber crime; complaints about women- and children-related crimes can be made anonymously.
sources.summary: India's official portal for reporting cyber crime, with the 1930 helpline for money lost to online scams.

sources.title: Decreto nº 7.962, de 15 de março de 2013 (contratação no comércio eletrônico)
sources.note: Read on 2 October 2026: applies the consumer code to online contracts, including respect for the right of withdrawal (art. 1, III); the consumer can withdraw through the same tool used to buy, and the supplier must confirm receipt at once and tell the card company so the charge is not billed or is reversed (art. 5).
sources.summary: Brazil's rules for buying online. They apply the consumer code's right of withdrawal to online purchases and say how to use it.
